newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BTP vol firm, action in downside puts.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BTP vol firm, action in downside puts.

text.p: BTP options volatility stood firm on Thursday after spiking higher the previous session on zigzagging Italian debt futures, traders said.

Italian futures burst higher on U.S. Treasuries' heels on Wednesday, but then lost their grip and retreated to near session lows. Analysts said the outlook was murky, leaving volatility at higher levels.
September downside puts were active, commanding an implied volatility of between 10.0-10.50 percent from around 9.0 percent a week ago, options traders said.
"For the next week or so we have to be wary of the downside," said a trader at an Italian bank in Milan.
Volume faltered on Thursday ahead of a public holiday in Italy on Friday to mark the Assumption Day, but some investors sought protection in downside puts.
September at-the-money strikes were quoted at 7.50 percent vol, while December was 7.10 bid and 7.45 offered.
By 1400 GMT, September BTP futures were 0.02 up on the day at 135.25 after having slipped from a peak of 135.93 on Wednesday.
Traders said the German Bundesbank's inflation warning on Wednesday when it said it would not shy away from raising rates if the upturn in prices continued, kept the Italian market on edge.
Most active puts were September 134.00 and 133.50 strikes, which traded at 8.90 percent volatility. The 132.00 put fetched 10.86 percent.
One strategy for bears was December out-of-the-money put spreads, for instance buying 106.50 and selling 105.50, the Italian trader said.
"You don't want to be short of volatility," he added.

Other traders on LIFFE said Eurolira options were quiet with volatility hovering at low levels. September Eurolira was at 9.50 percent and December stood at around 14, broadly unchanged from previous weeks.
